correctness.rationale: Import explicitly Chiclana’s exact identity n(ell_p^2(R))=M_p=max_{0<t<1}(t-t^{p-1})/(1+t^p) for p>2. With epsilon=2/p, eta=1-epsilon, t=e^{-2z/p}, the scalar objective becomes sinh(eta z)/cosh z; the stationarity equation tanh(eta z)tanh(z)=eta has a unique solution since the left side increases from 0 to 1, and objective vanishes at either endpoint. In y=t^p the equation epsilon(1+y^{2-epsilon})=(2-epsilon)(y+y^{1-epsilon}) gives y=Theta(epsilon), and expanding y^{1-epsilon}=y exp(-epsilon log y) yields y=epsilon/4+epsilon^2[1+log(epsilon/4)]/8+O(epsilon^3 log^2(1/epsilon)). Substitution with careful cancellation of mixed epsilon*y*log y terms gives n=1-[log(2p)+1]/p+[log^2(2p)+1]/(2p^2)+O(log^3(p)/p^3), and y=1/(2p)+[1-log(2p)]/(2p^2)+O(log^2(p)/p^3). Finite-dimensional duality transfers n to conjugate exponent p/(p-1). Independently evaluated the stationary root at p=100,1000,10000,100000,1000000 using high-precision root finding, tracking normalized remainders; source verify.py uses a separate optimization cross-check but finite numerics are not a proof of the big-O theorem.
